data: Asteroid · Jupiter Trojan · L5 · P-type · Binary primary

Primary of the largest known binary in the Jupiter Trojans — 113-km Patroclus paired with the 104-km Menoetius at a mutual separation of 680 km. The Iliadic pairing is deliberate: Patroclus and Menoetius are Achilles' beloved companion and his father, the two who in the epic fall together.

113-km P-type L5 Trojan asteroid — the primary of the largest known Trojan binary, paired with the nearly-equal-mass Menoetius. The 2033-03-02 Lucy encounter at 8.4 km/s closes the primary mission, marking the first ever spacecraft visit to a Trojan binary.
Patroclus is a binary system at L5 — trailing Jupiter by 60°. Lucy reaches it in 2033 to complete the first spacecraft tour of both Trojan clouds.
Five gravitationally-balanced spots in every two-body system where a small spacecraft can hover with almost no fuel — and where most modern deep-space observatories actually live.
